briefdescription.para: Predefined colour set, without escape sequences.

detaileddescription.para: Used by the formatters that write the messages of the checks, which are never coloured; all members are empty strings.

briefdescription.para: Predefined colour set, with green for pass and red for fail.

detaileddescription.para: Assigned by reporters that output to a colour-capable terminal; the members are, in order, the reset, pass, and fail ANSI escape sequences.

briefdescription.para: Appends the escape sequence of a control character.

detaileddescription.para: Writes the usual escape of the character (\\0, \\a, \\b, \\t, \\n, \\v, \\f, or \\r), or \\xHH for the other ones. Used for the characters of the messages and of the names that would otherwise reach the console and the output files unchanged. Defined in src/expression-formatter.cpp.

text
The text to append to.
c
The control character.
The usual escapes for the characters that have one; the other ones, including DEL, as \\xHH.

briefdescription.para: C++ header file with declarations for the µTest++ expression formatter.

detaileddescription.para: This header provides the expression_formatter class, which encapsulates all value-formatting logic used by the µTest++ framework. The class owns a std::string buffer and exposes operator<< overloads for every standard arithmetic type, character type, string, pointer, container, scoped enumeration, pair, tuple, optional, and framework expression type (see extension::is_op).

By consolidating the formatting operators into a single class (using the shared detail::append_number() helper for numbers), the reporter is relieved of those responsibilities, and detail::check_result can pre-format expression text, when initialised, without requiring reporter or test_case to be complete at that point.
The formatter shares the colour configuration of the owning reporter: comparator expressions are wrapped in pass/fail colour codes, which are empty strings unless the reporter enables colours.
All definitions reside within the micro_os_plus::micro_test_plus namespace.
This file is included by micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus.h, which is the header that the applications include.
